title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up an axiomatic framework, and much of it is crossed out and rewritten. Its probable purpose (chapter title 'Réseaux via découpages', 1986) is to encode combinatorially how a space is cut up by a family of 'cuts', and to recover a 'network' (réseau) structure from that incidence data. This sits within Grothendieck's tame-topology / 'géométrie modérée' programme of the Esquisse (1984).

The data are as follows.
(a) A set L of elements (cuts, curves, or points; the page does not say which). L carries a notion of 'modular' finite subset, generated by a reflexive, symmetric relation of 'relative modular position' on pairs. The pair {s,t} is modular iff s = t (the transcription reads '≠'; probably '=') or {s,t} ∈ S, a given set of pairs. Mod_f(L) denotes the finite modular subsets.
(b) For each T ∈ Mod_f(L), the 'modular complement' is C(T) = C_L(T) = { t ∈ L \ T | T ∪ {t} modular }. An earlier crossed-out draft instead put an equivalence relation R_T on an ambient V. The revision puts R_T on C(T). Its classes are called the 'connected components' of C(T), i.e. the regions of the complement of the cut system T.
(c) On the next page, each class A has a frontier Ȧ ⊂ T: the cuts that bound the region.

The margins record the evident monotonicity: if T ⊂ T' then C(T') ⊂ C(T). They also raise the question whether C_L(T) ≠ ∅.

The next page states the hoped-for economy of axioms. (c) should follow from (b). (b) should follow from the R_ε for ε in a basic family S_0, for example single cuts, where R_ε means 'which side of ε'. So the essential data would reduce to the modular-position relation plus, for each basic ε, a 'side' equivalence on C(ε). In modern terms this is a separation-system / oriented-matroid-like axiomatics: the chambers (regions) of an arrangement are recovered from the elementary sidedness relations.
errors: The text breaks off and nothing is proved on this page. The definition of a modular pair seems garbled ('s ≠ t ou {s,t} ∈ S'); the sensible reading is 's = t ou {s,t} ∈ S'.
The marginal question whether C_L(T) is non-empty is left open. Non-emptiness is not automatic from the data and would have to be an axiom.

ideas.what: Finite 'modular' (general-position) subsets of a set of cuts, generated by a binary relation of modular relative position
ideas.modern_name: Independence/general-position complex; flag complex of a compatibility graph
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6, but not this formalism

ideas.what: Modular complement C(T) with an equivalence relation whose classes are 'connected components' (regions), and a frontier map to T
ideas.modern_name: Chambers/regions of an arrangement and their walls; cell decomposition from incidence data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oriented matroids (Folkman–Lawrence 1978, Bland–Las Vergnas 1978); pseudoline arrangements (Levi, Grünbaum)

ideas.what: Hope that the whole region structure is determined by the 'side' relations for single basic cuts ε ∈ S_0
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of chambers from covectors/sign vectors; half-space/separation systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oriented matroid theory; Edelman's convex geometries; Dress's separation systems

missed.claim: An axiomatisation of 'networks obtained by cuttings' through modular cut systems, the components of their complements, and frontiers. It is aimed at a local-to-global reduction to elementary side relations, and is left as a programme.
missed.quote: ∀ T ∈ Mod_f(L), une relation d'équivalence R_T dans C(T) (dont les classes s'appellent les comp. connexes de C(T))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a possible independent anticipation of oriented-matroid / separation-space axiomatics. It is set inside Grothendieck's tame-topology programme, a link to o-minimal cell decomposition that is seldom made explicit. On this page, however, it consists only of definitions.

deep.surprise_reason: These are mostly crossed-out definitions of a combinatorial framework (modular subsets, complements, components). The framework resembles existing arrangement and oriented-matroid theory, and no result is stated.
transcription_corrections: The pair condition likely reads 's = t ou {s,t} ∈ S' rather than 's ≠ t'.
The insertion above R_T ('partiel mod[?]') is uncertain and may read 'partout déf.' or similar.
The marginal crossed-out text is plausibly 'Le complémentaire modulaire de T'. The definition in the body is written 'C_L(T)', with the original 'Comp' overwritten.
The crossed-out first (b) uses 'P_{f mod}(L)' and a relation R_T 'dans V'. The revision changes this to 'Mod_f(L)' and 'dans C(T)'.
